summary: A recent configuration change updated the orders service's INVENTORY_URL to port 8081 instead of 8080. This caused inventory connection timeouts, driving up error rates on both orders and gateway.

leads: Check `http_server_requests_seconds_count{outcome="SERVER_ERROR"}` for rising server errors in the orders service. (runbook:triage-high-error-rate)
Check gateway logs for "upstream request failed" (502) or "upstream request timed out" (504). (runbook:gateway-upstream)
Check if caller outgoing call latency rises together with callee server latency. (runbook:triage-high-latency)
triage.query: HighErrorRate gateway gateway: 21.2% of requests are failing; HighErrorRate orders orders: 45.75% of requests are failing

related.text:
- An alert like "orders: 12% of requests are failing".
- `http_server_requests_seconds_count{outcome="SERVER_ERROR"}` rising for one or
  more services.
- Callers log failed calls. The gateway logs "upstream request failed" (502) or
  "upstream request timed out" (504).
related.title: HighErrorRate: a service is returning 5xx

related.text:
- HighErrorRate on gateway. The gateway logs "upstream request timed out" (504,
  with `timeout_ms`) or "upstream request failed" (502).
- 504s: the upstream is slow, or the timeout is too short for its normal
  latency.
- 502s: the upstream is down or refuses connections (crash loop, rollout, pods
  not ready).
related.title: Gateway 502 and 504 responses

related.text:
- An alert like "orders: p95 latency is 2.3s".
- Callers' outgoing call latency (`http_client_requests_seconds`) rises together
  with the callee's server latency.
- Once latency passes a caller's timeout it turns into errors: the gateway
  returns 504 "upstream request timed out", and HikariCP logs "Connection is not
  available, request timed out after 2000ms".
related.title: HighLatency: p95 above one second

triage.summary: Requests to the orders service are failing for users and the gateway.

alerts.name: PodCrashLooping
alerts.summary: orders: container restarted 2.034 times in 10 minutes

hypotheses.summary: A configuration change incorrectly updated INVENTORY_URL to port 8081 while inventory listens on port 8080, causing connection timeouts and cascading failures in orders and gateway.

evidence.quote: orders: call inventory through its new internal port (#227)
evidence.shows: The deployment commit that changed the inventory URL configuration for orders.
The exact configuration diff changing the inventory port from 8080 to 8081.

evidence.quote: POST /orders failed: inventory POST /inventory/reserve failed: could not connect to inventory (connect timed out)
evidence.shows: The resulting connection timeout errors in orders due to targeting the incorrect port on inventory.

hypotheses.suggested_fix: Revert INVENTORY_URL in services/orders.yaml back to http://inventory:8080.

review.reason: The commit cited as the root cause occurred at 09:20:24Z, whereas the errors in orders already began at 09:10:27Z, making this change a subsequent event rather than the root cause.
